text:
olivia: Hey everyone, first day and my MacBook Pro arrived (M2, macOS 13.6). During setup the flow asked me to sign in with an Apple ID before the MDM profile could install and the 'Skip' button is greyed out. Is that expected?
it-support: Hi @olivia, welcome! Setup Assistant should not force a personal Apple ID for DEP/Automated Enrollment. Sounds like the device booted into consumer setup mode. Can you DM the serial?
olivia: Serial C02OLV12345. I followed the quickstart doc and tried to restart into recovery but I'm not sure which option to use.
it-support: Thanks. Quick triage: if the device shows the Apple ID prompt, it likely wasn't processed via ABM at pickup. Two paths: (A) we can reassign the device in Apple Business Manager and push an automated enrollment profile so Setup Assistant goes into MDM flow, or (B) if you'd rather not re-image, you can continue with a temporary local account, we can later wipe and reprovision. Which do you prefer?
olivia: I'd prefer to avoid wiping if possible. What happens if I continue without Apple ID?
it-support: You can create a local account and login, but you won't be managed by MDM until we re-enroll which usually requires re-running Setup Assistant (wipe) or using Apple Configurator with another Mac. For first-day dev access we can (1) temporarily add you to the remote dev SSH jumpbox and (2) grant a short-lived admin token so you can install tools.
olivia: Ok let's do that. Also the welcome email had an enrollment link — would that help now?
it-support: The enrollment link works only for user-initiated enrollment and requires the device to be in a non-DEP flow; it can work but it won't grant device attestation or ABM benefits. Given the Apple ID prompt, manual enrollment will still give you managed state but not device-affinity. If that's acceptable, install the profile from the link and let us know the output of `profiles show -type enrollment`.
olivia: Installed the profile via the link. `profiles show -type enrollment` output: "Enrollment Profile: id=manual-789, status=Enrolled, lastCheckin=now"

it-support: Great. You're managed now but note: Okta Device Trust and FileVault escrow usually require device-affinity for full automation. We'll do two things: 1) grant you a temporary admin token for 8 hours so you can install Homebrew/dev tools, 2) open a ticket to schedule a touchless re-provision to ABM in the next maintenance window so you get full device-affinity. Sound good?
emily: Approved 8h temporary admin for @olivia. Also adding a note: if anyone else gets an Apple ID prompt during setup, please DM IT with the serial so we can check ABM assignment before advising wipes.
olivia: Thanks! One more Q: FileVault didn't prompt during setup. If I enable now will my recovery key be escrowed even though this was a manual enrollment?
it-support: Yes, when you enable FileVault the MDM agent will attempt to escrow the personal recovery key to our KMS on next check-in. After you enable, reply here and we'll confirm.
olivia: Enabled FileVault and restarted.

macbot: [automated] FileVault personal recovery key escrowed to KMS for device C02OLV12345.

it-support: Confirmed the escrow. We're scheduling the ABM re-provision for tomorrow morning; that'll require a device wipe to re-enter DEP flow. We'll coordinate a 15-min window and give you remote help. Welcome to Redwood, @olivia!
joel: Welcome! If you need a dev image before reprovision, I can spin a cloud instance with your tooling.
olivia: Appreciate it, thanks everyone!
